verdict.rationale: Runpod's first-party docs describe network volumes as persistent storage that exists independently of compute and keeps data when Pods are terminated or scaled to zero. The volumes can be shared across machines and Runpod products, managed via CLI, and accessed through an S3-compatible API without launching a Pod. This directly covers datasets and checkpoints outliving a single GPU rental. Missing for 10: detailed documentation of the attach/mount workflow when creating a Pod, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can attach persistent network storage that survives instance teardown, so datasets and checkpoints outlive any single GPU rental

citations.quote: Network volumes provide persistent storage that exists independently of your compute resources. Data is retained when terminate or scale to zero.
Use them to share data across multiple machines and Runpod products.
This allows you to manage files on your network volumes without launching a Pod
You can manage Pods, Serverless endpoints, templates, network volumes, and models
